name: Free City of Hamburg
alt: Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg

predecessors.name: Holy Roman Empire (1260-1806)
predecessors.text: Hamburg 'became a sovereign state with the official title of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg' upon the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806

predecessors.name: First French Empire
predecessors.text: the city and Ritzebüttel, 'finally freed ... in 1814'

successors.name: German Empire
successors.text: the city-state as a member of the German Empire (1871-1918)

ledger.x: 1806: Hamburg becomes a sovereign state at the end of the Holy Roman Empire (Hamburg page: 'Upon the dissolution of the Holy Roman Empire in 1806 ... became a sovereign state with the official title of the Free and Hanseatic City of Hamburg').
1806: 'The cities of Hamburg and Bremen were occupied by the French army from 1806, following the end of the Prussian campaign' (Siege of Hamburg page).
13 December 1810: the occupation turns into annexation.
13 December 1810: Ritzebüttel goes with the city.
1814: Ritzebüttel at the Elbe mouth is again Hamburg's with the free city's restoration in May 1814.
1 January 1868: Hamburg takes over Lübeck's half of Bergedorf.

wars.name: Siege of Hamburg
wars.outcome: The siege ran from 24 December 1813 to 12 May 1814: the French garrison under Marshal Davout was besieged for over a year by Allied forces (mostly Russian, Swedish and German); it left Hamburg on 27, 29 and 31 May 1814 and Russian forces under General…

certainty.note: Cliopatria has no Hamburg shape before 1814 and no page gives a boundary; 1806-1810 uses the 1814 outline plus Ritzebüttel, 1811-1813 is French territory, 1814 is the restoration year.

A sovereign state of the German Confederation with defined territory, but the pages give no surveyed line; Bergedorf was a condominium with Lübeck to 1867, and Ritzebüttel and Neuwerk lay detached at the Elbe mouth.
